page: Microsoft Azure D48d_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 35 MB L3 cache. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of an 1843 GB SSD. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark results position the D48d_v4 in the average performance tier for most compute and memory tasks, with some notable strengths. The Passmark memory score is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2810.62, supported by a read-only small-block memory bandwidth of 2492.11 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 170.7 GB/sec for reads and 70.1 GB/sec for writes. Multi-core CPU performance is solid, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 42595.26 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11424.0. Database operations are handled efficiently, as evidenced by a Passmark database score of 15284.28 and a Redis SET throughput of 40.98 million operations per second. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in large-scale LLM text generation, yielding only 7.48 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D48d_v4 offers a balanced resource density by combining a high vCPU count with a substantial memory pool and a large, fast local SSD. This makes it a highly capable option for workloads requiring local scratch space without the overhead of external storage attachments. The instance is well-suited for general-purpose enterprise applications, relational databases, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and software compilation tasks. It is less optimal for heavy generative AI or large-scale LLM inference workloads due to the lack of GPU acceleration and lower text generation benchmark scores.
